intuition: A palindrome reads the same forward and backward. Start at its middle and compare the characters on either side. Keep moving outward while they match. Try every possible middle, including a gap between two characters, and keep the longest match.

Every palindrome is symmetric around a center. Odd lengths use one character as the center; even lengths use the gap between two characters. Starting with either kind, equal endpoint characters let us expand while keeping the entire enclosed substring palindromic. A mismatch ends just that center’s search.

Trying both centers at every index covers every possible palindrome. We keep only the best starting index and length rather than storing all candidates. The search is quadratic in the worst case, but it avoids the cubic work of rescanning each candidate’s interior.

steps: For s=cbbd, begin with best_start=0 and best_length=1, representing c.
The odd center at index 0 expands once, then hits the left boundary. Its valid length is 1.
At center 1, the odd choice yields b. The even choice starts at indices 1 and 2, where both characters are b.
Expand to indices 0 and 3. They contain c and d, so the expansion stops; the valid inner range is indices 1..2.
Compute length=3-0-1=2 and replace the best range with start 1, length 2.
The remaining centers cannot beat length 2, so slicing s[1:3] returns bb.

codeNotes.note: Offset zero represents an odd center; offset one represents an even center. Both are necessary because a single-character center can never discover bb.
The stopped pointers sit outside the valid palindrome. Removing those two outside positions explains the subtraction and avoids an off-by-one length.
Store coordinates during the search and allocate the answer only once. The exclusive slicing endpoint is starting index plus length.

keyDecision: Stop expanding when the characters differ or either position is outside the string.

concept.question: What happens when we grow a mirror outward from every possible center?
intuition: Trying every substring and checking it in both directions repeats many matching comparisons. A palindrome already has a stronger structure: each new outer pair must match around its center.

A palindrome is like a mirror placed in the middle of a word. Expand outward in matched pairs. The mirror can sit on one character or in a gap between two characters. Try both kinds of center and keep the widest successful expansion.
concept.observation: Stop an expansion at the first unequal pair or at the edge of the string.
approach: Choose a character center and a gap center.
Compare outward pairs until they differ or reach an edge.
Keep the longest matching continuous section across all centers.
concept.correctness: Every palindrome has either a character center or a gap center. Expanding from that center reproduces all of its matching pairs and may continue to a larger palindrome. Since every possible center is tested, the longest palindrome is among the expansions. Stopping at a mismatch cannot discard a longer palindrome with that same center.

complexity.explanation: There are roughly twice as many centers as characters. Each may expand across much of the string, giving quadratic work in the worst case. A few positions describe the expansion; the returned substring itself occupies output memory.

pitfalls: Try both odd and even centers.
Exclude the first mismatched outer pair.
Several equally long answers may be valid.

scenes.title: A one-letter mirror
scenes.narration: In cbbd, any single letter is a palindrome. Start with c as a length-one answer.
scenes.decision: A center need not have a matching outer pair to produce a valid one-letter palindrome.

scenes.title: A mirror in the gap
scenes.narration: The gap between the two b letters gives a matching pair bb, length 2.
scenes.decision: Even-length palindromes use a gap rather than a single central character.

scenes.title: The next outer pair breaks
scenes.narration: Outside bb are c and d. They differ, so stop. Other centers cannot improve on bb.
scenes.decision: The mismatched outer pair is excluded from the answer.
